Fix `plugins/catalog-backend/src/processing/formerEntityRefs.ts` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. Gate 3 S1 and S5, approved fixes. (1) S1: the rejected message must stay true for a claim rejected later. Replace it in formerEntityRefClaimErrors with exactly: Former entity ref '<ref>' was rejected because an entity from another source holds or held that ref. To clear this, remove the value from annotation backstage.io/former-entity-refs, then add it back once that entity is gone (keep the ${formerEntityRef} and ${ANNOTATION_FORMER_ENTITY_REFS} interpolations). (2) S5 cap: add a private constant MAX_FORMER_ENTITY_REFS = 20. In parseFormerEntityRefs, count distinct non-empty values whether or not they are valid. When a 21st distinct value appears, stop reading and push one InputError, after any per-value errors: `Annotation ${ANNOTATION_FORMER_ENTITY_REFS} holds more than ${MAX_FORMER_ENTITY_REFS} distinct former entity refs, so the extra ones were ignored`. The text carries no count and no value, so it stays stable and does not churn the result hash. Values past the cap are not returned, so they count as undeclared and any existing claim on them is removed as stale. This error is non-blocking like the others: it goes through the same errors array. (3) S5 truncation: add a private constant MAX_ECHOED_VALUE_LENGTH = 100, and in the invalid-value message echo the value cut to that many characters with `...` appended when it is longer.

instruction:
Fix `docs/features/software-catalog/life-of-an-entity.md` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. Gate 3 S1, S2 and S5, approved doc changes, under 'Renaming an Entity', following docs/contribute/doc-style-guide.md. (1) 'Claims on a Live Entity': say the check also runs on every later processing run, so a claim rejected because another source's entity holds the ref applies whether that entity was there first or arrived later. (2) Rewrite 'A New Entity Taking the Name': exact lookups always win. If the new entity has the same location key as the claimant, the claim becomes inactive with no error and takes effect again if that entity goes away. If it comes from another source, the claim is rejected the next time the claimant is processed, and stays rejected as described above. (3) Add a section '### Who Can Claim a Name' stating the trust model: the catalog does not prove that an entity ever held a former ref, so any entity author can claim any ref of the same kind, in any namespace, that nothing holds; old entity page and TechDocs links then open that entity with a renamed notice; a claim grants no permissions, because former refs are not used for relations or ownership and viewers still need read access to the target; there is no setting to turn this off; a claim on a free name is only rejected when the claimant is next processed after another source takes that name. (4) In 'Limits' add a bullet: an entity can declare at most 20 distinct former refs; the catalog reads them in annotation order, ignores the rest, and reports that on the entity.
